chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Jamila, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: 'Verily, sudden death is a lightening for the believer and a regrettable seizing of the disbeliever.'

key_terms.أَخْذَةُ أَسَفٍ: A seizing of regret — sudden death for the disbeliever is a devastating, regret-filled moment with no opportunity for repentance
key_terms.تَخْفِيفٌ: Lightening, relief, easing — used here to mean that sudden death spares the believer from the prolonged sufferings of terminal illness
key_terms.مَوْتُ الْفَجْأَةِ: Sudden death; an unexpected death that comes without warning or prolonged illness

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about sudden death for believers and disbelievers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) relays a prophetic tradition wherein the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) distinguishes the nature of sudden death for the believer versus the disbeliever. For the believing person, sudden death is described as a relief — sparing them from prolonged agony, fear, and the trials of a painful death. For the disbeliever, however, it is described as a 'seizing of regret' (أَخْذَةُ أَسَفٍ), indicating a sudden and unprepared departure that leaves no opportunity for repentance, making it a cause of grief and lamentation.
